main_import.use: Rank-one local Morse thimbles have a nonzero leading Gaussian coefficient. Analytic parameter Morse coordinates are applied only where the limiting local Hessian is invertible. The actual full-cut matching uses the adjacent logarithmic cutoff proof and retained/new uniform tail bounds.

retained_imports: NODAL_CENTER_LINE_DECAY.md supplies parameter-independent center-line carriers, a flat rank7 cut basis and normalized bounds, retaining full Gaussian means. NODAL_GAUSSIAN_CRITICAL_PROFILES.md supplies exact finite Milnor sums and escape scales. COERCIVE_GRADIENT_MOMENTS.md supplies pointwise complex gradient coercivity from the ordinary node and nonzero quadratic value. Compatible Hardt triviality and the formal-seed/actual-period bridge are reused with their prior source audits.
new_written_proof: For the strict triangle, a supporting normal to the off-axis edge has positive real parts on both Morse actions and negative real part on the critical-line action. A small perturbation orders the two positive growth rates. Their scalar leading coefficients are nonzero, so successive dominance removes both coefficients and the remaining five periods decay. This closes every center-line coefficient case.

For finite-critical profiles, the quantified set of admissible coercivity radii/constants is semialgebraic with nonempty fibers. Cell selection and one-variable algebraic growth give polynomial parameter bounds. Constrained compactified cut pairs and uniform finite-complexity area bounds give tails jointly polynomial in parameter and cut length. A logarithmic cutoff transfers the finite and escaping local Morse leading terms to the full flat basis.

Distinct finite P-values and nonzero quartic gamma make all nonzero positive-action polynomials distinct. On a generic ray their real growth orders separate. Growing coefficients vanish successively; bounded-action Morse periods and negative-action periods decay.
quartic_exception: gamma=d*e*m/(2*c)-l_T on h=f=0,e*c!=0, after swapping u,v when required. Opposite fourth roots have identical positive actions when gamma=0, so this boundary is not closed by the generic argument.
